texts.preamble: Da vs Bijender Sharma on 7 August, 2018 In The Court Of Samar Vishal, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 39713/2016 Date of Institution : 25.11.2002 Date of reserving judgement : 10.07.2018 Date of pronouncement : 07.08.2018 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus Sh Bijender Sharma S/o Late Sh. Bhu Dev Sharma, M/s Sharma Store, Near Madhu Medicos, Opposite Triveni Hospital, Karawal Nagar Road, Sadat Pur, Delhi R/o 4/2-128, Karawal Nagar Extension, Delhi-94 ... Accused Judgment: 1. texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of th e PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 23-10-2001 at about 12.00 noon the Food Inspector Ram Pratap Singh purchased a sample of 'Mustard Oil ', a food article for analysis from accused Bijender DA vs Bijender Sharma Sharma from the premises of M/s Sharma Store, Near Madhu Medicos, Opposite Triveni Hospital, Karawal Nagar, Sadat Pur, Delhi, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused Bijender Sharma was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling. The sample consisted of approximately 375 gms of 'Mustard Oil" ready for sale taken from open tin bearing no label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh Satnam Singh SDM/LHA. The sample was taken after proper mixing with the help of clean & dry measure, already kept in it by rotating it in all possible directions. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting them in three separate lean and dry bottles. Da vs Bijender Sharma on 7 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84234370/ 1 Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed. fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice am given to accused Bijender Sharma and the price of the sample was also given to him vide vendor's receipt dated 23-10-2001. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by FI were signed by accused Bijender Sharma and the other witness Sh. D.V. Singh, FI. Before the sample proceedings efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward then Sh. D.V.Singh, F.I joined as witness 3. One counter- part of the sample beating LHA Code No. SS/LHA/847 was also sent to Public Analyst Delhi in intact condition and two counterparts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found same not conforming to the standards as land down under the DA vs Bijender Sharma PFA Act and Rules. The report of the Public Analyst is es follows: "The sample does not conform to the standard because saponification and Iodine value exceed the prescribed maximum limit of 177 end 112 respectively" . 4. Further the vendor was selling the Mustard Oil in loose form i.e. in unpacked condition for human consumption which is prohibited in Delhi as per Gazetted Notification dated 27th August,1998. 5. It is the case of the complainant that accused Bijender Sharma was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Sharma Store, Near Madhu Medicos, Opposite Triveni Hospital, Karwal Nagar Road, Sadat Pur Delhi-94 at the time of the sampling and as such found to be in charge of and responsible for the day to day conduct of business of the above shop. 6. It is further stated that the accused has violated the Gazette Notification dated 27th August 1998 by the Food (Health) Authority in pursuance of the provision of clause (IV) of section 7 of PFA act, due to which sale of mustard oil in loose form i.e. in unpacked condition for human consumption is prohibited. Despite the above requirement of Gazette Notification dated 27th August, 1998, vendor was selling the the mustard oil in loose form and therefore violated the Gazette Notification dated 27th August, 1998 and also violated section 2(ia)(a)(b) and (m) of PFA Act. 7. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 25.11.2002 alleging DA vs Bijender Sharma violation of section 2(ia)(a)(b)&(m) of PFA Act as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. 8. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 25.11.2002. The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL, notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act being violation of Section Da vs Bijender Sharma on 7 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84234370/ 2 2(ia)(a),(b)&(m) of PFA Act, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 9. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 SDM Satnam Singh, PW-2 FI Suniti Kumar Gupta, PW-3 FI Ram Pratap Singh and PW-4 FA D.V. Singh. PW- 3 and PW-4 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh Satnam Singh. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 375 gms of mustard oil from the vendor which was lying in an open tin bearing no label declaration, dividing it into three equal parts by putting three separate clean and dry sample bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in Form VI Ex.PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C. The accused furnished his statement Ex.PW1/D. DA vs Bijender Sharma Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was deposited with the PA on 24.10.2001 vide receipt Ex.PW1/F and the two remaining counterparts of the sample in intact condition alongwith two copies of Memos in Form VII were deposited with LHA vide LHA receipt Ex.PW-1/E. Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW-1/G was received, according to which the sample found adulterated. During investigation, PW-3 FI Ram Pratap Singh sent letter Ex.PW3/A to STO Ward No. 74 and received its reply stating that no such firm was found registered with the Sales Tax. Thereafter, on completion of investigation, the complete case file alongwith documents were sent through LHA to the then Director PFA Shri K.S.Wahi, who granted consent for prosecution of accused after applying his mind vide Ex.PW1/H. Thereafter the present complaint Ex.PW1/J was filed before the Court. Then intimation letter Ex.PW2/A alongwith copies of PA's Reports were sent to the accused persons through post vide postal receipt Ex.PW2/B. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 10. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 31.10.2009 wherein the accused persons denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR 1999 SC 738], it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a) it annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned. 15. In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents. In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed as under:- (a) The accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt if on account of delay or lapse on the part of prosecution to institute a prosecution, the Director CFL is unable to analyse the sample because of delay or of the sample undergoes a change for this reason. (b) Once the Director has examined the sample and has delivered his certificate, under proviso to sub-section (5) of section 13 of the Act, the certificate is final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein. The prime argument of the Ld. Defence Counsel on the basis of which acquittal is sought at the threshold in this matter is thus, 'since there is variation of more than 0.3% in the reports of PA and CFL, the samples were not representative'. 20. In this regard, the defence strongly relies upon the judgement titled as Kanshi Nath v. State [2005(2) FAC 219], informing that the said ruling has been followed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in various other decisions. 21. This issue of variation was considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Delhi Administration vs Vidya Gupta Criminal Appeal No. 625 of 2018 dated 24.04.2018 wherein it was held that the finding of Hon'ble High Court in Kanshi Nath vs State and State vs Mahender Kumar & Ors, which hold that if in the comparison of reports of PA and the Director vast variations are found, then the samples are not representative, is improper. Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature, substance or quality which it purported or represented to be. Section 2(ia)(b) it has to be established that the food article contains any other substance which injuriously affect the nature, substance or quality thereof.
